explain.say: A seed is a baby plant packed with its own lunch, waiting. When conditions are right it wakes up and sprouts, and this is called germination.

explain.say: First the seed soaks up water and swells until its coat splits. Water switches on enzymes that turn the stored food into sugar the baby plant can use; it needs warmth and oxygen too.

faq.q: What does a seed need to sprout?
faq.a: Most seeds need water, warmth and oxygen. Light is not usually needed, because the seed lives on its stored food until its leaves reach the light, though a few small seeds, like some lettuces, do need light.
asks: What are the conditions for germination?

faq.q: Why does the root come out first?
faq.a: The root anchors the seedling and starts soaking up water, which the growing shoot will need. Getting a grip on the soil first also stops the seed being washed away.
asks: Which part grows first from a seed?

faq.a: Seed leaves, or cotyledons, are part of the seed. In beans they hold the stored food, and in many plants they turn green and make food until true leaves grow. Grasses like maize have one; beans have two.

faq.q: How long can a seed wait before sprouting?
faq.a: Many seeds stay dormant for months or years. In 2005 scientists sprouted a date palm seed about 2,000 years old, found at Masada in Israel.

faq.q: Does it matter which way up you plant a seed?
faq.a: No. The root senses gravity and turns to grow down, and the shoot turns to grow up, whichever way the seed lands.
asks: What if I plant a seed upside down?

facts: A Judean date palm seed about 2,000 years old was successfully sprouted in 2005.
The first part to emerge from a germinating seed is the radicle, the embryonic root.
Seeds live on stored food, mostly starch, oil or protein, until their leaves can make food.

quiz.say: Which of these does a bean seed NOT need to start sprouting?
quiz.show: Which of these does a bean seed NOT need to start sprouting?
quiz.why: Bean seeds sprout in dark soil, living on stored food; light matters later, for the leaves.
